subhead: The government held a seminar on the next budget bill on Monday. By proposing a limited bill, with no real deficit reduction and no major reforms, Lecornu hopes to secure decisive support from some Socialist MPs.

title: War becomes the new normal in the Strait of Hormuz
subhead: The renewed strikes between the United States and Iran on Monday, August 31, confirms that the conflict has become entrenched in these waters. Tehran's ability to use the blockade of this strategic artery as a deterrent is gradually weakening.

title: French YouTuber Lena Situations wraps up successful vlog series in sold-out Paris show
subhead: In front of an audience of 20,000, the French-Algerian content creator wrapped up the tenth and final season of her successful YouTube series 'August Vlogs' on Monday, August 31, with a show at the Accor Arena in Paris.

title: US sees rising opposition to Flock, a network of 120,000 vehicle-identifying cameras
subhead: Protests are mounting against Flock, a license plate detection system sold by a private company, which is widely seen as an intrusive threat to civil liberties. Over 60 cities have ended contracts with the company due to public pressure.

'No regulation exists:' Suez Canal becomes gateway for invasive species in the Mediterranean
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (6/6). The opening of a passage between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean led to migrations of 'Lessepsian' species, named after the canal's developer, Ferdinand de Lesseps. Their proliferation, which destabilizes ecosystems, has increased due to overfishing, pollution, coastal building and climate change.

title: How Céline Dion became the queen of Vegas (and is about to set Paris alight)
subhead: It was in Las Vegas that the Canadian superstar prepared the series of shows she will perform in Paris starting in September. She lived in Sin City for more than 20 years and reached the height of her career by reinventing the concept of a residency.

title: Will this summer's climate disasters push French politicians and citizens to act?
subhead: Heatwaves, wildfires and droughts, all intensified by climate change, do not lead to shifts in public attitudes without strong political will. Still, a sense of a need for protection and concrete measures is emerging.
